dispositions.1: certain — syntax-directed with no ambiguity (declarations, extends, imports, exports)
dispositions.0.5: low — overrides whose base could not be resolved across files
dispositions.0.6: DECLARED HESITATION — three distinct shapes, all deliberate: call-receiver roots (X10's tier, where `calls` names only the leaf so the receiver is named by nothing else), field-access roots, and whole-module forms (namespace import, re-export, CJS require/dynamic import — a namespace binds an object, not a declaration, so there is nothing to resolve TO: JD-J12/JD2b)
dispositions.0.85: high — field-access chain segments and template substitutions

confidenceTiers.note: M12 reports a bare `unknown` count for anything below 0.7. These are the tiers that count feeds, measured and named, so the number is auditable rather than merely reported.

declarations.arrow_function: Function symbol only when bound to a declarator; an inline argument arrow names nothing
declarations.assignment_pattern: default-value parameter name recorded, never a symbol
declarations.catch_clause: the caught parameter is a binding, recorded on the owner
declarations.class: Class symbol for a class EXPRESSION — owns members too (M49 W13)
declarations.class_declaration: Class symbol, and the scope owner for its members
declarations.export_clause: container for export names; never a symbol
declarations.field_definition: Property symbol; `#x` private form collapses to x
declarations.formal_parameters: parameters recorded on the owner, never symbols
declarations.function_expression: Function symbol when named or bound to a declarator
declarations.generator_function: Function symbol when named or bound to a declarator
declarations.import_clause: container for import specifiers; never a symbol
declarations.regex_pattern: NOT a declaration: a regex literal is a VALUE. Its pattern text is never a symbol, never a target, and never parsed for code — which is the zero-regex contract stated as a disposition rather than as a promise. Found by gate 1, which is the only reason this row exists: the name ends in `_pattern`, so the declaration-shape heuristic flagged it, and the correct answer was to account for it rather than to widen the heuristic until it stopped asking.
declarations.rest_pattern: rest parameter name recorded, never a symbol
declarations.variable_declarator: Constant for const, Variable for let/var; Function when the value is a function

readPositions.assignment-rhs: uses @0.9 — the value side of `a = b`
readPositions.call-receiver: uses @0.6 + metadata.callReceiver — the chain ROOT of a member callee
readPositions.field-access: uses @0.85 — `title.length` publishes the chain root and each segment
readPositions.object-key: no edge — a key is a name being DEFINED, not read

data.independence: Discovery reads the CORPUS and the GRAMMAR only. Neither the analyzer's tables nor the oracle is consulted for discovery, because a construct both of them forgot cannot appear as a disagreement — that is the X1 shape. The analyzer is consulted only for the probes.

moduleIdentity.family: javascript / typescript / svelte / vue emit no Module symbol; only clojure does
moduleIdentity.ruling: module identity is carried by the SOURCE of every exports/imports edge, which is the file's module name

orphanGap.disposition: DECLARED AND MEASURED — not closed by this gate; closing it is a separate change with its own blast radius
orphanGap.finding: JD3 (reviews/javascript/m60-deep-review-2026-09-26.md:209, '10.9% of real symbols are ownerless') is HISTORICAL, not falsified. It diagnosed ownerName coming only from scopeOwnerName, which reported class scopes only; the analyzer now derives the owner from containerOwnerName, which handles class expressions and object literals by their binding. The defect population measured here — object-literal members WITH a reachable binding that were not placed — is 0. Members with no binding (export default, return value, call argument, array element) are correctly ownerless by the analyzer's own documented contract.

objectLiteralMethods.ruling: 0 of the BOUND members are unplaced, so the containment contract holds for this shape. The 92/92 figure counted members that have no binding at all, which the contract places outside containment by design.

withoutBinding.disposition: correctly ownerless — no binding to name

orphanGap.population: class members (method/field definitions, including class expressions) and object-literal methods — the set the containment contract covers. Roots, function-locals and top-level declarations are EXCLUDED because no containment edge is claimed for them.

sample.selection: sorted, then evenly strided — deterministic and reproducible

limitations: Discovery is a CORPUS SCAN with a deterministic cap, not a proof about the language: a construct no corpus file spells is invisible to this gate and is reported as not seen rather than accounted for. The cap is published in `data.sample` (files per corpus, bytes per file) so what was read is auditable, and the selection is sorted-then-strided rather than random, so a rerun over the same corpora reads the same files.

This gate consults NEITHER the analyzer's tables NOR the oracle for discovery — that is the only reason it exists, since the differential compares two readings of the specification by one author and cannot see a construct both forgot (it reported coverage while the receiver of a member call was named by nothing). It answers 'does anybody account for this construct', not 'is this construct handled correctly'; the differential and the hand-audited corpus truth answer the second question.

The declared member-base table behind the reserved-base check is derived from the sample this artifact publishes rather than curated by hand, and gate `census-js-named-bases-verified` probes a leaf of every non-console base, so the table cannot rot into asserting suppression that no longer happens. A base absent from the sample is not asserted about at all.
title: javascript construct census — the check that consults neither the analyzer nor the oracle
